title: Volcano Explorer: inspect existing results and export a figure
description: Explore the real Regression example, synchronize the current style controls, distinguish visual thresholds from statistical testing, and save reproducible figure styles and exports.
objectives: Open the nested Volcano Explorer with the completed Regression guide family.
Synchronize initial controls through the verified Save style and Load style workaround.
Inspect point identities, effect and P-value axes, colour and reference lines without inventing new hits.
Restore a saved style and inspect vector PDF and PNG exports.
prerequisite: Extract Volcano_real_guide_family.zip and open its results folder. These are unchanged outputs from the downloaded-data Regression tutorial, not a new analysis or a complete project archive. One family contains 434 guides, outcome log_pred, minimum_wells_threshold=2, plus-one permutation P values and BH correction. Minimum raw P=0.005, minimum adjusted P=0.39454545454545453; zero significant at original alpha=0.05. Standardized marginal effects are not simultaneously fitted multivariable coefficients or log2 fold changes. The native initial style-control defect remains: displayed alpha=1e-6, multiplier=0 and log=False disagree with rendered .05/3/True. Before editing, Save style then Load that same style synchronizes controls. All 67 style fields survive the later roundtrip. Moving alpha to .5 puts nineteen adjusted values below that cutoff but preserves zero source significance flags; it is not new testing. Restore .05 and adjusted_p_value before export. An explicit effect cut .1 with multiplier 3 gives lines at +/-0.3. Actual point coordinates, identities, source flags and support colours are checked. Nominal 7-by-5-inch, 150-DPI settings export a tightly cropped 492.536-by-348.485-point PDF and 1026-by-726-pixel PNG. The PDF has embedded fonts and no raster images; labels were visually rechecked. Some GUI labels remain clipped and the application warns about white marker outlines on light paper. Annotation merging, broken axes, localization and control-MAD rules are not certified by this example. The preserved recording was made with spaCR 1.5.0.4; its screen, widget and renderer source bytes still match the current checkout. No new regression, GPU, AI provider request, application modification, biological validation or publication. API: spacr.volcano_style.VolcanoStyle and render_volcano.

scenes.narration: Open Regression and its nested Volcano Explorer. This lesson belongs under Regression in the submodule section. The explorer reads completed results; it does not rerun the analysis. We use the real downloaded-data Regression example, with a companion archive containing the exact result tables and recorded figure styles.

Choose Open results and select the extracted results folder. Each point here is one guide from a single family of four hundred thirty-four tests, using the same outcome and minimum-well rule. Do not pool different correction families. No guide is significant at the original adjusted-P cutoff of zero point zero five.

Before changing any setting, use Save style to save the actual rendered style, then Load style from that same file. In this build the initial controls disagree with the figure, and editing immediately can pull incorrect defaults into the plot. This normal save-and-load workaround synchronizes them; it does not fix the application.

After reloading, confirm alpha zero point zero five, multiplier three, and the negative-log transform. Some setting labels remain clipped in this build, so check the values and saved JSON. The horizontal axis is standardized marginal effect, not log-two fold change or a coefficient from a simultaneously fitted multivariable model.

Click an existing point to inspect its source row. The selected guide has raw P zero point zero zero five, but adjusted P about zero point three nine. Its large marginal effect and four supporting wells do not make it significant. Use the identity and source fields rather than guessing from a dot's position.

Switching the vertical column to raw permutation P changes the plotted quantity, not the analysis. Small raw values do not replace the family-adjusted values. Restore adjusted P afterwards. The saved source significance flags remain unchanged; the explorer is a reader and figure editor, not a new statistical test.

The negative-log-ten switch changes how P values are displayed. With it on, smaller P values appear higher; turning it off displays the original values. We restore the transformed adjusted-P view here. Always read the axis label, and do not confuse the transform with a different multiple-testing correction.

For demonstration, moving alpha to zero point five moves the reference line. Nineteen adjusted values fall below that new P cutoff, but none gains a new source significance flag. This is not a valid claim of nineteen discoveries. Restore the original zero point zero five before exporting or interpreting this example.

An explicit effect cutoff of zero point one combines with multiplier three, placing vertical lines at minus and plus zero point three. Check the multiplier rather than reading the cutoff field alone. An effect threshold does not replace statistical correction. Restore Auto after this exercise; no result-table values are rewritten.

Colour by wells with guide displays actual support from the source table. It is not a confidence score or proof of accuracy. Return to the original significance colours before the final export. Optional annotation joins and other layouts need their own validation and are outside this verified example.

Set the intended figure size, font sizes and resolution, then inspect the result. Here the nominal size is seven by five inches at one hundred fifty dots per inch. Tight bounding-box cropping changes the final dimensions. A readable exported figure does not mean every native settings label fits this window.

Save the final style as JSON. After a temporary marker-size change, Load style restores every recorded style field. Keep that file with the original result table so another session can reproduce the appearance. Style settings describe presentation; they do not establish that a different regression or significance test was run.

Export PDF and PNG re-render the figure rather than capture the screen. Our PDF contains vector marks and embedded fonts; inspect labels, contrast and the warning about white marker outlines on light paper. Original data remain unchanged. Python provides VolcanoStyle and render_volcano for the same rendering workflow, without a GPU or AI provider.
